sourceHtml:
Coding agents now build working web apps: a dashboard, a product page, a prototype that a product team wants to try. The fastest way to review that work is to open the app, use it, ask for a change, and check the result. That loop works well when the app keeps running where the agent edits it, so each change shows up in the browser within seconds. When the app must be copied out and deployed somewhere else first, every change waits for a deployment, and the review slows down to that pace.

Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is a platform to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale, with your choice of agent framework and foundation model (FM). AgentCore runtime, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, runs each agent session in its own isolated microVM. With Session endpoints, you can open an app running in that session from your own browser. Session Endpoints give each session an authenticated URL that forwards each request’s HTTP method, path, query string, and body, and WebSocket connections, to the ports you allow. You can watch the page update as the agent saves each file.

In this post, you deploy a coding agent that keeps a Vite website running in its session, then open one local page with a chat on the left and the live website on the right. You ask the agent to switch the site to a dark color theme, follow its steps as they stream in, and watch the website change without a refresh. Finally, you look at what happens internally: a second port in the same session, and the requests the Session endpoint refuses.

The complete sample, including the notebook this post follows, is in the 14-remote-access folder of the agentcore-samples GitHub repo.

How Session endpoints work

Each session gets its own Session endpoint, and six details shape how you use it.

You choose which ports it reaches. You set allowedPorts when you call CreateAgentRuntime: 1–5 entries, each a single port or a range within 8000–12000, excluding the reserved platform ports. Allowing a port doesn’t start a server, so your application must listen on it, bound to 0.0.0.0.

The URL arrives with the session. The InvokeAgentRuntime response carries it in the X-Amzn-Bedrock-AgentCore-Runtime-Session-Endpoint-Url header, which SDKs that model it expose as sessionEndpointUrl.

Every request is authenticated. For a runtime that uses AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM), each HTTP request, HTTP/2 stream, and WebSocket handshake carries a Signature Version 4 (SigV4) signature. The caller also needs bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntimeProxy on the runtime and its runtime endpoint. For a runtime with an inbound JSON Web Token (JWT) authorizer, each request carries a bearer token instead. Knowing the URL doesn’t grant access.

The host name selects the port. Your client connects on port 443 regardless of the target port, and a prefix on the host name chooses the port inside the session:

https://8090--<session-endpoint-id>.runtime.bedrock-agentcore.<region>.on.aws/index.html
https://8081--<session-endpoint-id>.runtime.bedrock-agentcore.<region>.on.aws/status

It carries the protocols your server speaks. HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 requests, including server-sent events and gRPC, and WebSocket connections all pass through. This walkthrough uses HTTP/1.1 and WebSocket.

It’s scoped to one session. The URL needs credentials on every request and lasts only as long as the session, so use it to build, test, and review what your agent produces. To serve an app to your users, deploy it to a hosting service such as AWS Amplify Hosting.

A browser can’t add a SigV4 signature or a bearer token to the requests a page makes on its own, so the Session endpoint client in the bedrock-agentcore SDK can open a local endpoint on your machine. Your browser opens http://localhost:8088, and the local endpoint adds your credentials to each request and WebSocket handshake before forwarding it.

A Session endpoint is different from a runtime endpoint, which AgentCore runtime already provides. Use a runtime endpoint, such as DEFAULT, to reach your agent, which controls which version of it callers will reach. InvokeAgentRuntime calls resolve through it, so you can keep development and production on different versions and promote or roll back without changing callers. Use a Session endpoint to see what your agent runs in its session, such as a web preview. It’s an authenticated URL that reaches only the ports you allow, works with whichever version the session runs, and stops working when the session ends. For complete documentation, refer to Connect to runtime sessions through a session endpoint.

Solution overview

The sample has four parts. A coding agent runs in the session on port 8080 and edits the website’s files with four tools: list, read, write, and edit. The agent starts a Vite development server on port 8090, which serves the website and pushes each saved change to the browser over its hot-reload WebSocket. On your machine, PreviewApp serves the preview page, sends your prompts to InvokeAgentRuntime, and opens a local endpoint for the website. As Figure 1 shows, the preview page loads the website from the Vite development server on port 8090 through the local endpoint and the Session endpoint, and sends your prompts through InvokeAgentRuntime to the agent on port 8080. The numbers show the order of the steps for one request.

Figure 1: Solution architecture

Before step 1, PreviewApp has already called InvokeAgentRuntime once to start the session, which starts the agent and the Vite development server. PreviewApp read the Session endpoint URL from that response and opened a local endpoint for port 8090. The numbered steps in Figure 1 then follow one request for a change:

  1. The site pane of the preview page loads the website from the local endpoint on localhost:8088. The local endpoint adds your credentials to each request and the WebSocket handshake, and forwards them to the Session endpoint. The Session endpoint checks the signature and the port against allowedPorts, then forwards them to the Vite development server on port 8090. The page keeps the Vite hot-reload WebSocket open.
  2. You send a prompt from the chat pane. PreviewApp sends it to InvokeAgentRuntime as a standard AWS API call signed with your AWS credentials, and the runtime delivers it to the agent on port 8080. The agent’s steps stream back to the chat pane as it works.
  3. The agent calls Claude Haiku 5.5 in Amazon Bedrock to decide what to change.
  4. The agent reads the site’s files and saves the ones it changes. The Vite development server serves those files and watches them for changes.
  5. When a file is saved, Vite pushes the change over the WebSocket opened in step 1, back through the Session endpoint and the local endpoint, and the site pane updates without a refresh.
  6. From the notebook, PreviewApp reads the agent’s /status route on port 8081 through the same Session endpoint. Only the port changes.

Port 8080 isn’t in allowedPorts, because InvokeAgentRuntime reaches the agent without going through the Session endpoint.

Prerequisites

To follow the walkthrough, you need:

  • An AWS account in an AWS Region where AgentCore runtime Session endpoints are available, with credentials configured.
  • Permissions to create an AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) role, upload to Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3), and create a runtime, plus bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntime and bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntimeProxy on that runtime and its DEFAULT runtime endpoint. For details, refer to IAM permissions for AgentCore runtime.
  • Python 3.10 or later, with bedrock-agentcore 1.25.2 or later and boto3 1.43.122 or later.
  • Git, to clone the sample repo, and a Jupyter environment, such as JupyterLab or Visual Studio Code with the Jupyter extension, to run the notebook.
  • Access to Claude Haiku 5.5 in Amazon Bedrock. For model availability by Region, refer to Regional availability by models.
  • Node.js 22 or later with npm, which the deployment script uses to package the agent and the website.

The sample deploys the agent as a zip file in Amazon S3 with direct code deployment for Node.js, so you don’t need Docker or an Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository. Session endpoints work with microVM runtimes, not with the Instances compute type, and Session endpoint URLs are reachable over public HTTPS. AWS PrivateLink isn’t supported for inbound connections.

Deploy the agent and its website

First, you deploy the runtime, and the configuration you choose here decides which ports the Session endpoint can reach. The deployment script bundles the agent into one file, adds the website and its dependencies for the runtime’s Linux on Arm64 system, uploads the zip to Amazon S3, and creates the runtime.

The following excerpt from deploy.py shows the two settings that matter for this post. protocolConfiguration says where the agent listens for InvokeAgentRuntime, and allowedPorts lists the ports the Session endpoint can reach: 8090 for the website and 8081 for the agent’s status route. Port 8080 isn’t in the list, because InvokeAgentRuntime reaches the agent without it. For the port and path settings, refer to Configure your agent’s serving port and invocation path.

agentRuntimeArtifact={"codeConfiguration": {
    "code": {"s3": {"bucket": code_bucket(), "prefix": S3_PREFIX}},
    "runtime": "NODE_22",
    "entryPoint": ["app.js"],
}},
protocolConfiguration={"serverProtocol": "HTTP", "port": 8080, "path": "/invocations"},
allowedPorts=[{"port": 8090}, {"port": 8081}],

The website’s Vite configuration makes the development server reachable from the Session endpoint. It listens on 0.0.0.0 at port 8090 and doesn’t restrict the Host header (server.allowedHosts is true), because requests arrive under a host name the runtime assigns rather than localhost. The Session endpoint authenticates every request before it reaches the server, so the server doesn’t need its own host check.

To deploy the runtime:

1. Clone the sample repo and change to the sample folder:

git clone https://github.com/awslabs/agentcore-samples.git
cd agentcore-samples/01-features/02-host-your-agent/01-runtime/03-advanced/16-session-endpoints

2. Open session_endpoints_preview.ipynb from the sample folder.

3. Run the install cell, which installs the Python dependencies.

4. Run the %run deploy.py cell. Deployment takes a few minutes, mostly waiting for the runtime to reach the READY status.

Open the preview

With the runtime ready, you start the preview. One call does three things: it starts a session (which starts the website), opens a local endpoint for port 8090, and serves the preview page on localhost:8087.

from preview_app import PreviewApp

app = PreviewApp().start()
print("Open", app.url)

Inside start(), the calls that use Session endpoints are short. The first InvokeAgentRuntime call returns the URL in a response header, session_endpoint_url reads it, and the Session endpoint client opens a local endpoint for port 8090:

answer = client.invoke_agent_runtime(
    agentRuntimeArn=runtime_arn, runtimeSessionId=session_id,
    payload=json.dumps({"prompt": ""}).encode(), contentType="application/json",
)
endpoint = client.session_endpoint_client(session_endpoint_url(answer))
local = endpoint.open_local_endpoint(port=8090, local_port=8088).start()

To open the preview:

  1. Run the cell that starts PreviewApp.
  2. Open the printed link, http://localhost:8087, in your browser.

The page shows the website on the right, served from port 8090 in the session, and a short guide with suggested requests on the left.

Ask the agent for a change

Now you ask for a change and watch it arrive. Each prompt goes to the agent through InvokeAgentRuntime. The agent reads the files it needs, writes the ones it changes, and reports each step as it happens. When a file is saved, the Vite development server pushes the change over its WebSocket, through the Session endpoint and the local endpoint, and the website updates in place.

To ask for a change:

  1. On the preview page, choose Switch this website to a dark coffee-house color theme.
  2. Follow the agent’s steps in the chat pane as it reads and saves files.
  3. Watch the site pane. It changes when the agent saves the stylesheet, and a banner names the file the change came from.

The following video shows the preview page while the agent works through several requests. Choosing a suggested request sends it to the agent, the chat pane lists each file the agent reads and saves, and the site pane on the right updates without a refresh, from the dark theme to a green Order ahead button.

Figure 2: The preview page as the agent works

The steps stream because the agent answers with server-sent events when you ask it to. You can send the same prompts from Python with app.ask, which reads the stream with iter_events from the bedrock-agentcore SDK. The open page updates in the same way:

for event in app.ask("Make the Order ahead button green"):
    if "step" in event:
        print("  ", event["step"])
    elif "done" in event:
        print(event["done"]["reply"])

The output of this Python script should resemble the following:

   Looking at the site's files
   Reading src/main.js
   Reading src/style.css
   Reading index.html
   Saved src/style.css
The Order ahead button is now green instead of brown, with white text kept for contrast. You can see it in the hero section, just below the "Small batch coffee, roasted every morning" heading at the top of the page.

Reach a second port in the same session

The website isn’t the only server you can reach. The agent serves /status on port 8081, which lists each prompt and the files it changed. The same Session endpoint reaches it, and the only difference is the port argument.

status = app.endpoint.request("GET", "/status", port=8081)
print("GET /status on port 8081: HTTP", status.status)
for edit in status.json()["edits"]:
    print("  ", edit["prompt"], "->", ", ".join(edit["files"]))

The output of this Python script should resemble the following:

GET /status on port 8081: HTTP 200
   Make the Order ahead button green -> src/style.css

What the Session endpoint refuses

When the runtime refuses a request, it answers with an HTTP status, an empty body, and an error code in a response header, so you can tell its refusals from errors your application returns. The notebook sends a request to a port outside allowedPorts and a request without credentials, and the runtime refuses both with 403 AccessDenied.

The following table lists the refusals you’re likely to meet while you build with Session endpoints.

Request Response from the runtime
A port that isn’t in allowedPorts 403 AccessDenied
A request without valid credentials 403 AccessDenied or 401 AuthenticationRequired
An allowed port with nothing listening on it 502 PortNotReachable
A URL whose session no longer exists 404 SessionNotFound

How access to your session is protected

The runtime removes its own authentication headers before it forwards a request, so the website doesn’t receive your signature. Requests are recorded in AWS CloudTrail as InvokeAgentRuntimeProxy events, with the event source bedrock-agentcore.amazonaws.com. The local endpoint acts with your credentials, so it limits who can use it. It listens on 127.0.0.1 only, answers only requests addressed to its own local address, and refuses WebSocket connections opened by pages from other origins. Run the local endpoint only while you use the preview. For more information, see Log session endpoint requests in CloudTrail.

The access controls don’t separate the website from the agent. Both run in the same session, so give the execution role only the permissions the agent needs. If the runtime replaces the session’s compute, open connections close, and the agent’s edits might not survive unless the session uses persistent storage. Refer to File system configurations for AgentCore runtime if you need the files to outlast the compute.

The agent’s file tools resolve every path inside the site folder and refuse paths outside it, so a prompt can’t make the agent change other files in the session. If other people can send prompts to your coding agent, consider Amazon Bedrock Guardrails to filter harmful prompts and responses, and review the agent’s changes before you publish them.

Clean up

To avoid ongoing charges, stop the preview and delete the resources the sample created. The website the agent edited lives in the session, so it goes with the session.

To clean up:

1. Run the stop cell, and press Enter when the notebook asks. This stops the preview page, the local endpoint, and the session.

2. Run the %run cleanup.py cell, which deletes the runtime, the uploaded code, and the IAM role.

Conclusion

Session endpoints give you authenticated access to the applications in an AgentCore runtime session from your own tools over HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and WebSocket, on the ports you allow. In this post, you deployed a coding agent with a Vite website in its session, opened the live website in your browser through a local endpoint, asked the agent for a dark theme, and watched the change arrive as the agent saved the file. You also reached a second port in the same session and confirmed what the Session endpoint refuses.

To go further, run the notebook with your own site in the site folder, or change the agent’s tools to match how your coding agent works. For the full set of options, including port ranges, OAuth, HTTP/2, and gRPC, refer to Connect to runtime sessions through a session endpoint.

To change the port or path that InvokeAgentRuntime uses in your own agent, refer to Configure your agent’s serving port and invocation path. If your agent also needs to run build or test commands in the same session, refer to Execute shell commands in AgentCore runtime sessions. To deploy your own Node.js agent from a zip file the way this sample does, refer to Direct code deployment for Node.js. For everything else the service offers, start with Host agent or tools with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime, and find more examples in the agentcore-samples GitHub repo.

About the author

translation.html:
编程智能体现在已经能构建可运行的 Web 应用：仪表板、产品页面，或产品团队想要试用的原型。审查这些成果最快的方式，就是打开应用、实际使用、提出修改要求，然后检查结果。当应用持续运行在智能体编辑它的环境中时，这个循环就能顺畅运转，每次修改都会在几秒内显示在浏览器中。如果必须先把应用复制出来并部署到其他地方，每次修改都要等待部署，审查也就随之放慢。

Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 是一个用于大规模构建、连接和优化智能体的平台，你可以自行选择智能体框架和基础模型（FM）。AgentCore 运行时是 Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 的一项功能，它在独立的隔离 microVM 中运行每个智能体会话。借助会话端点，你可以从自己的浏览器打开该会话中运行的应用。会话端点为每个会话提供一个需要身份验证的 URL，将每个请求的 HTTP 方法、路径、查询字符串和请求体，以及 WebSocket 连接转发到你允许的端口。智能体每保存一个文件，你都能看到页面随之更新。

在本文中，你将部署一个编程智能体，让它在自己的会话中持续运行一个 Vite 网站，然后打开一个本地页面，左侧是聊天区，右侧是实时网站。你将要求智能体把网站切换为深色主题，跟随实时传回的步骤查看它的操作，并观察网站无需刷新就发生变化。最后，你将查看内部发生的情况：同一会话中的第二个端口，以及会话端点会拒绝的请求。

完整示例（包括本文所使用的 notebook）位于 agentcore-samples GitHub 仓库的 14-remote-access 文件夹中。

会话端点的工作原理

每个会话都有自己的会话端点，以下六个细节决定了它的使用方式。

由你选择它可以访问哪些端口。 调用 CreateAgentRuntime 时，你需要设置 allowedPorts：包含 1–5 个条目，每个条目可以是 8000–12000 范围内的单个端口或一段端口范围，但不能包含平台保留端口。允许某个端口并不会启动服务器，因此你的应用必须在该端口上监听，并绑定到 0.0.0.0。

URL 会随会话一同返回。InvokeAgentRuntime 响应通过 X-Amzn-Bedrock-AgentCore-Runtime-Session-Endpoint-Url 响应头携带该 URL，对此响应头建模的 SDK 会将其作为 sessionEndpointUrl 暴露。

每个请求都要进行身份验证。对于使用 AWS Identity and Access Management（IAM）的运行时，每个 HTTP 请求、HTTP/2 流和 WebSocket 握手都携带 Signature Version 4（SigV4）签名。调用方还需要对该运行时及其运行时端点拥有 bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntimeProxy 权限。对于使用入站 JSON Web Token（JWT）授权器的运行时，每个请求则携带 Bearer 令牌。知道 URL 并不意味着拥有访问权限。

主机名决定端口。无论目标端口是什么，客户端都通过端口 443 连接，而主机名上的前缀用于选择会话内部的端口：

https://8090--<session-endpoint-id>.runtime.bedrock-agentcore.<region>.on.aws/index.html
https://8081--<session-endpoint-id>.runtime.bedrock-agentcore.<region>.on.aws/status

它支持服务器使用的协议。HTTP/1.1 和 HTTP/2 请求（包括服务器发送事件和 gRPC），以及 WebSocket 连接都能通过。本演练使用 HTTP/1.1 和 WebSocket。

它的作用范围仅限于一个会话。访问此 URL 的每个请求都需要凭证，且 URL 只在会话存续期间有效，因此适合用来构建、测试和审查智能体生成的内容。如果要向用户提供应用，请将其部署到 AWS Amplify Hosting 等托管服务。

浏览器本身无法为页面发出的请求添加 SigV4 签名或 Bearer 令牌，因此 bedrock-agentcore SDK 中的会话端点客户端可以在你的计算机上开启一个本地端点。浏览器打开 http://localhost:8088，本地端点会在转发每个请求和 WebSocket 握手之前，为其添加你的凭证。

会话端点不同于 AgentCore 运行时已经提供的运行时端点。使用 DEFAULT 等运行时端点可以访问智能体，该端点控制调用方将访问智能体的哪个版本。InvokeAgentRuntime 调用通过它进行解析，因此你可以让开发环境和生产环境使用不同版本，并在不更改调用方的情况下升级或回滚。使用会话端点则可以查看智能体在会话中运行的内容，例如 Web 预览。它是一个需要身份验证的 URL，只能访问你允许的端口，适用于会话所运行的任何版本，并在会话结束时失效。完整文档请参阅通过会话端点连接到运行时会话。

解决方案概览

此示例包含四个部分。编程智能体在会话中的端口 8080 上运行，并通过四个工具编辑网站文件：列出、读取、写入和编辑。智能体在端口 8090 上启动一个 Vite 开发服务器，提供网站内容，并通过其热重载 WebSocket 将每次保存后的更改推送到浏览器。在你的计算机上，PreviewApp 提供预览页面，将你的提示发送到 InvokeAgentRuntime，并为网站开启本地端点。如图 1 所示，预览页面通过本地端点和会话端点，从端口 8090 上的 Vite 开发服务器加载网站，并通过 InvokeAgentRuntime 将你的提示发送到端口 8080 上的智能体。图中的数字表示一次请求中各步骤的顺序。

图 1：解决方案架构

在步骤 1 之前，PreviewApp 已经调用过一次 InvokeAgentRuntime 来启动会话，从而启动智能体和 Vite 开发服务器。PreviewApp 从该响应中读取会话端点 URL，并为端口 8090 开启本地端点。随后，图 1 中的编号步骤展示一次修改请求的处理过程：

  1. 预览页面的网站窗格从 localhost:8088 上的本地端点加载网站。本地端点为每个请求和 WebSocket 握手添加你的凭证，并将它们转发到会话端点。会话端点检查签名，并根据 allowedPorts 检查端口，然后将它们转发到端口 8090 上的 Vite 开发服务器。页面保持 Vite 热重载 WebSocket 连接打开。
  2. 你从聊天窗格发送提示。PreviewApp 将其作为使用你的 AWS 凭证签名的标准 AWS API 调用发送到 InvokeAgentRuntime，运行时再将其传递给端口 8080 上的智能体。智能体工作时，其操作步骤会以流式方式返回聊天窗格。
  3. 智能体调用 Amazon Bedrock 中的 Claude Haiku 5.5，决定要做哪些修改。
  4. 智能体读取网站文件，并保存它修改过的文件。Vite 开发服务器提供这些文件，并监视它们的变化。
  5. 文件保存后，Vite 通过步骤 1 中建立的 WebSocket 连接推送更改，经由会话端点和本地端点返回，网站窗格无需刷新即可更新。
  6. 在 notebook 中，PreviewApp 通过同一个会话端点读取智能体位于端口 8081 上的 /status 路由。只有端口发生变化。

端口 8080 不在 allowedPorts 中，因为 InvokeAgentRuntime 无需经过会话端点就能访问智能体。

前提条件

要完成本演练，你需要：

  • 一个 AWS 账户，使用支持 AgentCore 运行时会话端点的 AWS 区域，并已配置凭证。
  • 拥有创建 AWS Identity and Access Management（IAM）角色、上传到 Amazon Simple Storage Service（Amazon S3）以及创建运行时的权限，同时对该运行时及其 DEFAULT 运行时端点拥有 bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntime 和 bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntimeProxy 权限。详情请参阅 AgentCore 运行时的 IAM 权限。
  • Python 3.10 或更高版本，以及 bedrock-agentcore 1.25.2 或更高版本和 boto3 1.43.122 或更高版本。
  • 用于克隆示例仓库的 Git，以及用于运行 notebook 的 Jupyter 环境，例如 JupyterLab 或安装了 Jupyter 扩展的 Visual Studio Code。
  • 访问 Amazon Bedrock 中 Claude Haiku 5.5 的权限。有关模型在各区域的可用性，请参阅各模型的区域可用性。
  • Node.js 22 或更高版本，以及 npm，部署脚本会用它来打包智能体和网站。

此示例使用 Node.js 直接代码部署，将智能体作为 Amazon S3 中的 zip 文件进行部署，因此不需要 Docker 或 Amazon Elastic Container Registry（Amazon ECR）仓库。会话端点适用于 microVM 运行时，不适用于 Instances 计算类型，会话端点 URL 可通过公共 HTTPS 访问。入站连接不支持 AWS PrivateLink。

部署智能体及其网站

首先，部署运行时，你在此处选择的配置将决定会话端点可以访问哪些端口。部署脚本将智能体打包为一个文件，添加适用于运行时 Arm64 架构 Linux 系统的网站及其依赖项，将 zip 文件上传到 Amazon S3，然后创建运行时。

以下摘自 deploy.py 的片段展示了与本文相关的两个设置。protocolConfiguration 指定智能体在哪个位置监听 InvokeAgentRuntime，allowedPorts 则列出会话端点可以访问的端口：8090 用于网站，8081 用于智能体的状态路由。端口 8080 不在列表中，因为 InvokeAgentRuntime 无需通过它就能访问智能体。有关端口和路径设置，请参阅配置智能体的服务端口和调用路径。

agentRuntimeArtifact={"codeConfiguration": {
    "code": {"s3": {"bucket": code_bucket(), "prefix": S3_PREFIX}},
    "runtime": "NODE_22",
    "entryPoint": ["app.js"],
}},
protocolConfiguration={"serverProtocol": "HTTP", "port": 8080, "path": "/invocations"},
allowedPorts=[{"port": 8090}, {"port": 8081}],

网站的 Vite 配置使会话端点能够访问开发服务器。服务器在 0.0.0.0 的端口 8090 上监听，并且不限制 Host 请求头（server.allowedHosts 为 true），因为请求使用的是运行时分配的主机名，而非 localhost。会话端点会在每个请求到达服务器之前验证其身份，因此服务器不需要自行检查主机名。

部署运行时的步骤如下：

1. 克隆示例仓库，并切换到示例文件夹：

git clone https://github.com/awslabs/agentcore-samples.git
cd agentcore-samples/01-features/02-host-your-agent/01-runtime/03-advanced/16-session-endpoints

2. 打开示例文件夹中的 session_endpoints_preview.ipynb。

3. 运行安装单元格，安装 Python 依赖项。

4. 运行 %run deploy.py 单元格。部署需要几分钟，主要是在等待运行时进入 READY 状态。

打开预览

运行时准备就绪后，即可启动预览。一次调用会完成三件事：启动会话（从而启动网站）、为端口 8090 开启本地端点，以及在 localhost:8087 上提供预览页面。

from preview_app import PreviewApp

app = PreviewApp().start()
print("Open", app.url)

在 start() 中，使用会话端点的调用很简短。第一次 InvokeAgentRuntime 调用在响应头中返回 URL，session_endpoint_url 读取该 URL，然后会话端点客户端为端口 8090 开启本地端点：

answer = client.invoke_agent_runtime(
    agentRuntimeArn=runtime_arn, runtimeSessionId=session_id,
    payload=json.dumps({"prompt": ""}).encode(), contentType="application/json",
)
endpoint = client.session_endpoint_client(session_endpoint_url(answer))
local = endpoint.open_local_endpoint(port=8090, local_port=8088).start()

打开预览的步骤如下：

  1. 运行启动 PreviewApp 的单元格。
  2. 在浏览器中打开输出的链接 http://localhost:8087。

页面右侧显示由会话中的端口 8090 提供的网站，左侧显示一份简短指南，其中包含建议尝试的请求。

要求智能体进行修改

现在，提出修改要求，并观察修改生效。每条提示都通过 InvokeAgentRuntime 发送给智能体。智能体读取所需文件，写入修改后的文件，并在每个步骤发生时报告进展。文件保存后，Vite 开发服务器通过 WebSocket 推送更改，经由会话端点和本地端点，网站便会原地更新。

提出修改要求的步骤如下：

  1. 在预览页面上，选择将此网站切换为深色咖啡馆配色主题。
  2. 在聊天窗格中跟随智能体的操作步骤，查看它读取和保存文件的过程。
  3. 观察网站窗格。智能体保存样式表时，网站会发生变化，并显示一条横幅，指出此次更改来自哪个文件。

以下视频展示了智能体处理多个请求时的预览页面。选择一条建议请求即可将其发送给智能体，聊天窗格会列出智能体读取和保存的每个文件，右侧的网站窗格则无需刷新即可更新，从深色主题一直到绿色的“提前下单”按钮。

图 2：智能体工作时的预览页面

这些步骤之所以能以流式方式传回，是因为在你提出相应要求时，智能体会通过服务器发送事件作答。你也可以在 Python 中使用 app.ask 发送相同的提示，它会使用 bedrock-agentcore SDK 中的 iter_events 读取流。已打开的页面也会以同样的方式更新：

for event in app.ask("Make the Order ahead button green"):
    if "step" in event:
        print("  ", event["step"])
    elif "done" in event:
        print(event["done"]["reply"])

这段 Python 脚本的输出应与以下内容类似：

   Looking at the site's files
   Reading src/main.js
   Reading src/style.css
   Reading index.html
   Saved src/style.css
The Order ahead button is now green instead of brown, with white text kept for contrast. You can see it in the hero section, just below the "Small batch coffee, roasted every morning" heading at the top of the page.

访问同一会话中的第二个端口

网站并不是唯一可以访问的服务器。智能体在端口 8081 上提供 /status，其中列出每条提示及其修改的文件。同一个会话端点即可访问它，唯一的区别是端口参数。

status = app.endpoint.request("GET", "/status", port=8081)
print("GET /status on port 8081: HTTP", status.status)
for edit in status.json()["edits"]:
    print("  ", edit["prompt"], "->", ", ".join(edit["files"]))

这段 Python 脚本的输出应与以下内容类似：

GET /status on port 8081: HTTP 200
   Make the Order ahead button green -> src/style.css

会话端点会拒绝哪些请求

运行时拒绝请求时，会返回 HTTP 状态码、空响应体，以及响应头中的错误代码，因此你可以区分运行时的拒绝响应与应用返回的错误。notebook 会向 allowedPorts 之外的端口发送一个请求，并发送一个不带凭证的请求，运行时会以 403 AccessDenied 拒绝这两个请求。

下表列出了使用会话端点进行构建时可能遇到的拒绝情况。

请求 运行时的响应
不在 allowedPorts 中的端口 403 AccessDenied
不带有效凭证的请求 403 AccessDenied 或 401 AuthenticationRequired
已允许但没有服务监听的端口 502 PortNotReachable
会话已不存在的 URL 404 SessionNotFound

会话访问如何受到保护

运行时在转发请求之前会移除自身的身份验证请求头，因此网站不会收到你的签名。请求会在 AWS CloudTrail 中记录为 InvokeAgentRuntimeProxy 事件，事件源为 bedrock-agentcore.amazonaws.com。本地端点使用你的凭证执行操作，因此会限制哪些主体可以使用它。它仅监听 127.0.0.1，只响应发往自身本地地址的请求，并拒绝由其他源的页面发起的 WebSocket 连接。仅在使用预览时运行本地端点。更多信息请参阅在 CloudTrail 中记录会话端点请求。

这些访问控制并不会将网站与智能体隔离开。两者运行在同一个会话中，因此只应授予执行角色智能体所需的权限。如果运行时替换了会话的计算资源，已打开的连接会关闭，智能体的修改也可能丢失，除非该会话使用了持久性存储。如果你需要让文件在计算资源被替换后仍然保留，请参阅 AgentCore 运行时的文件系统配置。

智能体的文件工具会将所有路径解析到网站文件夹内，并拒绝该文件夹之外的路径，因此提示无法让智能体修改会话中的其他文件。如果其他人可以向你的编程智能体发送提示，请考虑使用 Amazon Bedrock Guardrails 过滤有害的提示和响应，并在发布前审查智能体所做的修改。

清理

为避免持续产生费用，请停止预览，并删除示例创建的资源。智能体编辑的网站位于会话中，因此会随会话一同删除。

清理步骤如下：

1. 运行停止单元格，并在 notebook 提示时按 Enter 键。这会停止预览页面、本地端点和会话。

2. 运行 %run cleanup.py 单元格，删除运行时、已上传的代码和 IAM 角色。

结语

会话端点让你能够从自己的工具出发，通过 HTTP/1.1、HTTP/2 和 WebSocket，在允许的端口上以经过身份验证的方式访问 AgentCore 运行时会话中的应用。在本文中，你部署了一个在会话中运行 Vite 网站的编程智能体，通过本地端点在浏览器中打开实时网站，要求智能体应用深色主题，并观察到智能体保存文件时修改随即生效。你还访问了同一会话中的第二个端口，并确认了会话端点会拒绝哪些请求。

如果想进一步尝试，可以将自己的网站放入 site 文件夹后运行 notebook，或者修改智能体的工具，使其符合你的编程智能体的工作方式。有关完整选项，包括端口范围、OAuth、HTTP/2 和 gRPC，请参阅通过会话端点连接到运行时会话。

要更改你自己的智能体中 InvokeAgentRuntime 使用的端口或路径，请参阅配置智能体的服务端口和调用路径。如果智能体还需要在同一会话中运行构建或测试命令，请参阅在 AgentCore 运行时会话中执行 shell 命令。要像本示例一样通过 zip 文件部署自己的 Node.js 智能体，请参阅 Node.js 直接代码部署。要了解该服务提供的其他功能，请从使用 Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 运行时托管智能体或工具开始，并在 agentcore-samples GitHub 仓库中查找更多示例。
